title: Heuristic rank shift after scheduler merge causing burst latency increase
creator: Jonas Kim
description: A recent scheduler merge unintentionally changed the default heuristic weighting for kernel ranking. Over several production bursts this caused the runtime to prefer a quantized kernel variant for mid-length generation paths, which increased tail latency (p95/p99) and caused transient capacity reduction due to KV cache miss amplification.
impact: Incidents observed across multiple clusters in us-west-2 during peak traffic windows. p95 latency regressed from ~120ms to ~280ms and p99 from ~350ms to ~1.1s on affected models. Dedicated pools experienced degraded throughput (10-18% drop) and several customer routes tripped soft SLO alerts. No data loss; some customers reported timeouts from application-level retries.
timeline: 2025-02-12 03:15 UTC - Pager alerted: cluster us-west-2 inference-pool p99 spike on model 'rw/gpt-medium-open'
2025-02-12 03:22 UTC - On-call (Aisha) started triage, pulled scheduler logs and kernel-selection traces
2025-02-12 03:45 UTC - Identified correlation between newly merged scheduler heuristics (PR #6281) and sudden kernel ranking shifts
2025-02-12 04:05 UTC - Emergency rollback of scheduler heuristics to previous defaults deployed to canary nodes
2025-02-12 04:30 UTC - Canary metrics normalized; rolled rollback to remaining nodes by 06:00 UTC
2025-02-13 09:00 UTC - Post-incident deep dive with serving runtime, scheduler, and QA teams
2025-02-20 10:30 UTC - Implemented temporary safety gate to prevent heuristic deltas > 0.15 without manual review
2025-03-01 16:00 UTC - Ongoing: comprehensive test coverage and canary plan in progress (owner: Aisha)
detection: Automated latency SLO alerting (Per-route p99), supplemented by runtime kernel-selection anomaly detector that flagged >25% shift in kernel distribution for an otherwise unchanged workload.
root_cause: The scheduler merge adjusted the relative score components used when ranking kernel candidates. A minor parameter change increased the weight of a 'memory-footprint' term which biased selection toward lower-memory quantized kernels for mid-length sequences. Those kernels have higher KV cache miss sensitivity in our serving patterns, which amplified tail latency during bursts. The change was untested for mixed-concurrency profiles and escaped unit and e2e canaries because the canary traffic distribution did not exercise the mid-length sequence pattern at production scale.
mitigation: Rolled back heuristic defaults to prior safe values across affected clusters (hotfix v2.11.1)
Added emergency routing rule to prefer fused kernels for models with historical KV cache sensitivity until fixes land
Enabled transient admission control to smooth bursts to dedicated pools while root cause investigation proceeded
Notified impacted customers and provided mitigation guidance for application retry/backoff
completed_actions: Customer notifications sent to Top-20 affected tenants (2025-02-12)
Short-term safety gate implemented in scheduler config (2025-02-20)
Added observability dashboard for kernel-distribution by route and sequence-length bucket
long_term_actions: Rework heuristic scoring to separate memory-footprint multiplier and KV-cache-sensitivity term (owner: runtime-team, estimate: 8)
Add e2e canary with synthetic mixed-concurrency, mid-length sequence profiles that mirror production percentiles (owner: qa-infra, estimate: 5)
Implement a kernel-selection regression test that runs on every scheduler PR and fails on >10% distribution shift (owner: scheduler-team, estimate: 3)
Introduce automatic fallback policy: if route-level p99 increases >2x within 5 minutes after a heuristic tweak, auto-revert and open an incident (owner: platform-sre, estimate: 5)
Benchmark quantized kernel variants for KV-cache miss sensitivity and publish performance profiles to model catalog (owner: perf-research, estimate: 8)
Schedule a retrospective to refine merge review checklist to include kernel-distribution impact analysis (owner: eng-managers, due_date: 2025-03-10, estimate: 2)
notes: Design decision: we accepted a small memory-footprint bias during the merge to improve node utilization; trade-off analyses underweighted KV-cache sensitivity.
Review feedback: PM and SRE asked for a canary plan that includes sequence-length percentiles before merging future heuristic changes (action added to long_term_actions).
Actionable insight: canary traffic must include replayed production traces with realistic concurrency to catch second-order selection effects.
